title: How would you estimate how many piano tuners work in Chicago?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many piano tuners work in Chicago?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: The most famous sizing question of all, first popularised by the physicist Enrico Fermi. It is a chain of five reasonable guesses. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many piano tuners work in Chicago?

The approach

Pianos × tunings per year ÷ tunings one tuner can do per year.

Tip: If you are unsure of a number, say your assumption and why. A reasoned guess beats a confident invention.

Step by step

  1. People in Chicago: 2.7M
  2. ÷ 2.5 people per household
  3. × 5% households with a piano
  4. × 1 tuning per piano per year
  5. ÷ 1,000 tunings one tuner does per year (4 a day, 250 days)

That gives about 54 piano tuners.

Does it make sense?

Schools, churches and concert halls add some pianos, so the true number might be a little higher.

Include commercial pianos without double-counting

The household estimate suggests roughly 54 full-time-equivalent tuners. A first adjustment is to include schools, theatres, places of worship and recording studios. If those add an illustrative 8,000 instruments, each tuned twice a year, that creates 16,000 extra tuning jobs. At 1,000 jobs per tuner, roughly 16 more full-time equivalents are required.

But workload is not perfectly uniform. Travel, repair work, cancellations and piano type can reduce the number of tunings a technician completes daily. A technician who spends half of working hours doing repairs cannot also complete the assumed 1,000 tunings per year.

Use this as a reminder to separate number of instruments, annual service frequency and effective technician capacity. Estimating a profession from demand is usually stronger than guessing how many practitioners you see in a city.
